# Anti-slop filter for AI coding agents: rules against generic AI-looking UI and copy

Curated by Skill Harbor — @miqdadbadjuber's anti-slop filter for AI coding agents: a rules system loaded always to stop generic, recognizable AI-slop output before it ships. Part 1 is a diagnostic scan of the telltale patterns (generic blue-purple gradients, excessive glassmorphism, monotonous hero→CTAs→feature-grid layouts, em dashes, generic CTAs, AI buzzwords, fake statistics, fabricated trust claims, Lucide-icon-everywhere). Part 2 is the meat — 38 mandatory rules in three tiers: Hard Gate (absolute — no em dashes in agent copy, mobile must be perfect, no fabricated numbers or testimonials, no dead interactive elements, required empty/loading/error states, WCAG AA contrast, keyboard navigability, no building features via CSS-patch scripts, design direction required before building), Purpose-Gate (color, gradients, icons, typography, badges, glassmorphism, glow, animations, illustrations are allowed only with a stated purpose, written down, with dose caps), and Quality Locks (no template layouts, max 2-3 core colors plus 1 accent, every decision must have a one-line reason). Part 3 adds liveliness: three dials every design must set (ENERGY, RHYTHM, MOTION) and a Design Read declaration. Two usage modes — during (rules applied while building, ending in a Delivery Gate PASS/FAIL report) or after (numbered audit of an existing project, fix only approved findings). Ships with a first-run install wizard (pointer block in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md, per-concern sub-skills...
